# renderpdf-js Create PDFs from HTML, images or code, and merge or split existing PDFs. - Version: 0.6.1 - License: MIT - Homepage: https://github.com/MichalekJan93/renderPDF.js#readme - Repository: git+https://github.com/MichalekJan93/renderPDF.js.git - Weekly downloads: 1453 - Dependents: 0 - Created: 2026-10-25T12:46:24.740Z - Updated: 2026-10-31T18:33:42.846Z ## Keywords - pdf - html - browser - typescript - html-to-pdf - image-to-pdf - tiff-to-pdf - pdf-generation - pdf-merge - pdf-split ## Dependencies | Package | Version | | --- | --- | | @pdf-lib/fontkit | ^1.1.1 | | html-to-image | ^1.11.13 | | pdf-lib | ^1.17.1 | | utif2 | 4.1.0 | ## Dev Dependencies | Package | Version | | --- | --- | | @playwright/test | ^1.64.1 | | @types/node | ^26.6.5 | | @types/pngjs | ^6.0.5 | | pdfjs-dist | ^6.4.299 | | pixelmatch | ^8.0.0 | | pngjs | ^7.0.0 | | typescript | ^6.0.3 | | vite | npm:@voidzero-dev/vite-plus-core@1.4.0 | | vite-plus | 1.4.0 | ## Version History | Version | Published | Deps | | --- | --- | --- | | 0.0.0-stage | 2026-10-25T12:46:24.740Z | 0 | | 0.1.0 | 2026-10-25T12:47:42.479Z | 3 | | 0.2.0 | 2026-10-26T07:56:37.651Z | 4 | | 0.2.1 | 2026-10-26T09:00:41.681Z | 4 | | 0.3.0 | 2026-10-26T10:38:42.889Z | 4 | | 0.4.0 | 2026-10-27T08:17:04.380Z | 4 | | 0.5.0 | 2026-10-27T10:02:26.960Z | 4 | | 0.5.1 | 2026-10-27T18:33:58.274Z | 4 | | 0.6.0 | 2026-10-29T09:58:48.641Z | 4 | | 0.6.1 | 2026-10-31T18:33:42.689Z | 4 | --- ## README # RenderPDF.js **Create PDFs from HTML, images or code, and merge or split existing PDFs.** npm version CI MIT License RenderPDF.js is a JavaScript and TypeScript library for creating PDF documents, converting HTML and images, and working with existing PDF pages. It runs locally, without a conversion server. HTML exports use the browser's layout, keep text selectable and split content across pages. Document creation and PDF composition also work in Node.js, without a DOM. **Experimental.** The full browser suite targets Google Chrome. Focused HTML export tests also pass in Microsoft Edge, Playwright Firefox and Playwright WebKit, including PDF downloads, page mapping, selectable Unicode text and local raster comparisons. A separate manual export passed in Safari 26.2. These are bounded tests, not a general HTML/CSS compatibility guarantee. Supported behavior and limits are described below. ## Features - Create documents with text, images, vector graphics, links and form fields. - Merge PDFs, extract selected pages and split documents without rasterizing them. - Export supported HTML/CSS with selectable text and automatic pagination. - Convert PNG/JPEG and multipage TIFF files to PDF. - Add repeated table headers, page text, page numbers and document properties. - Use the DevExtreme PDF exporter through an optional compatibility adapter. - ESM package with TypeScript declarations, cancellation and conversion progress. See the API guide for methods, coordinate conventions and compatibility limits. The changelog records what changed in each published version, where and why. ## Getting started ```sh npm install renderpdf-js ``` For browser applications, use an ESM bundler such as Vite. The playground provides HTML upload/editing, JSON options, a live preview, export diagnostics and timed RenderPDF.js/jsPDF comparisons from a source checkout. ## Measured HTML comparison We compared the source build at `78fe8c1` with jsPDF 4.2.1 `html()` in headless Brave 147 on one Apple M4 Pro (October 2026). Both used A4, 24 CSS px margins and the same explicit font bytes for each input. Times are medians of five exports through Blob serialization; bold marks the better measured result. | Test | RenderPDF.js | jsPDF | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------: | ---------------------: | | 24 short fixtures (up to 4 pages): faster median | **21/24** | 3/24 | | 24 short fixtures: smaller PDF | **22/24** | 2/24 | | 16 one-page fixtures: closer browser pixels | **16/16** | 0/16 | | 200-row directory: time / PDF bytes | 1.21 s / 405,837 B | **0.68 s / 320,758 B** | | 1,000-row inventory, matched fonts: time / PDF bytes | 1.74 s / **415,956 B** | **1.64 s** / 620,478 B | Both exporters retained all 460 text markers in the short documents, although marker page placement differed in four. The longer examples were separate runs: PDF.js found all 200 complete directory IDs and 1,000 complete inventory names in RenderPDF.js output, while one ID and one name were incomplete in the inspected jsPDF outputs. The visual count covers only one-page cases compared at equal scale. These are results for the linked source build and these fixtures on one machine; 0.6.1 is the first npm release containing that build. ## Create a document ```ts import { createDocument } from 'renderpdf-js'; const document = await createDocument({ unit: 'mm', format: 'A4' }); const page = document.addPage(); page.drawText('Invoice', { x: 20, y: 25, fontSize: 18 }); page.drawRectangle({ x: 20, y: 35, width: 170, height: 20, stroke: '#333333' }); const pdf = await document.toResult(); await pdf.download('invoice.pdf'); ``` Coordinates start at the top-left; text `y` is its baseline. Font sizes always use points. The document API works without a DOM. Built-in Helvetica, Times and Courier cover basic text; provide TTF/OTF bytes in `fonts` for characters outside their limited sets. Fonts accept bytes, bare base64 or a font data URL. A variable TTF is accepted only at its upright default axes and declared default weight. Fonts are prepared before drawing. After `toResult()`, the document is immutable. Use `pdf.toUint8Array()` or `pdf.toBlob()` outside the browser; `download()` is a browser action. ## Combine and split PDFs ```ts import { mergePDFs, extractPDFPages, splitPDF } from 'renderpdf-js'; const combined = await mergePDFs([firstFile, secondFile], { flattenForms: true }); await combined.download('combined.pdf'); const selected = await extractPDFPages(firstFile, [3, 1]); const individualPages = await splitPDF(firstFile); ``` Inputs can be `File`/`Blob`, `ArrayBuffer`, `Uint8Array` or a completed export result. Page numbers are one-based. Pages retain their native text, vectors, sizes and rotation. `flattenForms: true` turns ordinary prepared AcroForm appearances into page paint before composition; the default still rejects interactive fields. XFA, signed, encrypted PDFs and unsupported destinations fail explicitly. Flattening removes interactivity. Document-level bookmarks, signatures and metadata are not merged. See the composition limits. ## DevExtreme integration `createJsPDFAdapter()` provides the synchronous drawing and text measurement contract used by the DevExtreme PDF exporter. Supply fonts when creating it, pass the result as `jsPDFDocument`, then **await** `save()` or `output('blob')`. The adapter covers the tested exporter contract; it does not emulate every jsPDF plugin or its synchronous serialization. The API guide includes an example and the optional integration test command. DevExtreme is not a dependency of this library. ## HTML usage Select a connected element and export it. Font files are optional: ```ts import { renderPDF } from 'renderpdf-js'; const source = document.querySelector('#invoice'); if (!source) throw new Error('Invoice element was not found.'); const pdf = await renderPDF(source, { format: 'A4', margin: 24, }); for (const warning of pdf.warnings) { if (warning.code === 'FONT_SUBSTITUTED') console.warn(warning.message); } await pdf.download('invoice.pdf'); ``` Without `fonts`, the library bundles the licensed `RenderPDF Base` Noto Sans regular, bold and italic faces (SIL OFL license). If the source requests a face outside this base family or its available weights and styles, export continues and returns a `FONT_SUBSTITUTED` warning in both `pdf.warnings` and `onWarning`. This is a diagnostic for the application, not a thrown error. A connected source keeps its browser layout: substituted PDF glyph widths and wrapping can differ from the visible element. Use `renderHTML` when a copied document may be laid out again with the substitute face. If a substituted text node is inside a raster region, direct `renderPDF` rejects with `RASTER_FAILED` instead of combining a bitmap in the original font with PDF text in the substitute font; `renderHTML` can relayout its isolated copy. For `renderPDF`, the bundled fallback registers up to three reusable `FontFace` objects in the source document's `FontFaceSet` for that document's lifetime; the source DOM is unchanged. `renderHTML` owns a temporary iframe and releases its font registrations when the export finishes. For exact font output, supply licensed TTF/OTF bytes and ensure the source CSS uses the same family. Choose `fontMismatch: 'error'` to reject any missing face: ```ts import { registerFont, renderPDF } from 'renderpdf-js'; const source = document.querySelector('#invoice'); if (!source) throw new Error('Invoice element was not found.'); const response = await fetch('/fonts/MyFont-Regular.ttf'); if (!response.ok) throw new Error('The document font could not be loaded.'); const regular = await registerFont({ family: 'Document Sans', data: await response.arrayBuffer(), }); const pdf = await renderPDF(source, { fonts: [regular], fontMismatch: 'error', }); ``` Register every family and style used by the source, including italic faces. Available static weights follow CSS nearest-face matching: a requested weight of `600` can select a registered `700` face. A regular-only family does not silently stand in for bold or italic text: strict mode throws `MISSING_FONT`, while fallback mode reports `FONT_SUBSTITUTED`. TTF/OTF data can be bytes, bare base64 or a font data URL. Variable TTF files are supported only at their upright default axes and declared default weight; other axis values, system fonts, WOFF/WOFF2 and font collections remain unsupported. Disable optical sizing for a variable font with an `opsz` axis so browser and PDF outlines use the same instance. The selected face must contain every character in its text run; there is no automatic per-glyph fallback. A missing character fails with `MISSING_GLYPH`, even in font fallback mode. Keep the source connected and unchanged during export. `registerFont({ ..., document: source.ownerDocument })` registers a face in an iframe's own `FontFaceSet`; the same handles belong in that source's `renderPDF` options. The default preserves source width and fails when it exceeds the page's content width (about **745.7 CSS pixels** for A4 with default margins). `fit: 'width'` instead keeps the browser's original wrapping and uniformly reduces PDF paint and page mapping. ### Convert an HTML string `renderHTML(fullHtmlDocument)` also works without font files. It creates a temporary isolated document and lays it out with the bundled base face when a requested CSS family is unavailable. To supply exact fonts, page bands and layout options: ```ts import { renderHTML } from 'renderpdf-js'; const pdf = await renderHTML(fullHtmlDocument, { fonts: [{ family: 'Document Sans', data: fontBytes }], sourceWidth: 1200, fit: 'width', orientation: 'auto', fontFallback: 'Document Sans', header: { height: 36, html: '
Account statement
' }, footer: { height: 28, left: 'Printed by: Example', right: 'Page {pageNumber}/{pageCount}' }, }); ``` The default `isolation: 'iframe'` accepts a full HTML document. Use `isolation: 'shadow'` for a fragment. Both run in a temporary sandboxed iframe; their DOM and font faces are released after export. `sourceWidth` is the browser layout width before PDF fitting. In fallback mode, `renderHTML` changes the copied elements' CSS family before browser layout and reports `FONT_SUBSTITUTED`. This cannot preserve an unprovided system font such as Tahoma. With supplied fonts, `fontFallback` selects a registered substitute family. HTML header/footer fragments live in separate shadow roots: include their CSS inline or in each fragment. Scripts, frames, templates, customized built-ins, active attributes and refresh metadata are rejected. Ordinary image and CSS URLs may still trigger browser requests. ## Standalone image files `imageToPDF` accepts a `File`, `Blob`, `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array`. It detects the format from the file contents and requires no HTML element or fonts. ```ts import { imageToPDF } from 'renderpdf-js'; const fileInput = document.querySelector('#image'); const file = fileInput?.files?.[0]; if (!file) throw new Error('Select a PNG, JPEG or TIFF file.'); const pdf = await imageToPDF(file, { format: 'A4', margin: 24 }); await pdf.download('document.pdf'); ``` PNG and JPEG produce one page. Each main TIFF frame produces a page in file order. Images are centered and scaled to fit within the margins, preserving their aspect ratio; small images can be enlarged. TIFF/EXIF orientations, including mirrored orientations and PNG `eXIf`, are applied. JPEG compressed bytes are preserved. Image text remains a bitmap; there is no OCR. See image format limits for supported TIFF profiles. TIFF support applies to this API; HTML ` ` elements accept PNG/JPEG. ## API parameters The tables list public conversion and document settings, accepted values and defaults. HTML and standalone-image dimensions use **CSS pixels**: `1 px = 0.75 PDF pt`. Custom paper dimensions include margins. Document drawing uses its selected `unit`; font sizes in that API always use points. Required values have no implicit substitute. ### `renderPDF(element, options)` | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `element` | Existing browser layout. Keep it connected and stable until completion. | Positive-size `HTMLElement`, including one in an accessible same-origin iframe. | Required. | | `fonts` | Exact faces used by source text and page bands. | Array of `registerFont()` handles belonging to the source document. | Bundled `RenderPDF Base` Noto Sans faces. | | `fontMismatch` | Missing CSS face policy; fallback returns `FONT_SUBSTITUTED`, error throws `MISSING_FONT`. | `'fallback'` or `'error'`. | `'fallback'` without fonts or with `fontFallback`; otherwise `'error'`. | | `fontFallback` | Preferred substitute family in fallback mode; direct DOM layout remains unchanged. | Family included in `fonts`, or bundled `RenderPDF Base`. | Bundled `RenderPDF Base` when fallback is selected. | | `format` | Paper size including margins. | `'A4'`, `'A3'`, `'Letter'`, or `{ width, height }` with finite positive CSS-pixel dimensions. | `'A4'`. | | `orientation` | Selects paper axes without reflowing the source. | `'portrait'`, `'landscape'`, or `'auto'` based on measured source width. | `'portrait'`. | | `margin` | Empty edges; must leave a positive content area. | Finite nonnegative number, or `{ top, right, bottom, left }` in CSS pixels. | `24` on each edge. | | `fit` | Uniformly shrinks wide content and page mapping, retaining browser wrapping. | `'none'` or `'width'`. | `'none'`; excess width rejects. | | `pageBreak` | Controls supported authored CSS fragmentation hints. | `'css'` or `'auto'` for geometry alone. | `'css'`. | | `repeatTableHeaders` | Repeats supported native `thead` on continuation pages. | `true` or `false`. | `false`. | | `header` | Reserves an additional repeated band above body content. | Text line, text slots or connected HTML; see band fields below. | Omitted. | | `footer` | Reserves an additional repeated band below body content. | Same forms as `header`. | Omitted. | | `fallback` | Controls automatic selection of safe local raster regions. | `'auto'` or `'strict'`; strict requires explicit `data-raster` for effects needing capture. | `'auto'`. | | `strictCss` | Rejects selected unsupported decoration instead of omitting it; independent of raster planning. | `true` or `false`. Default omission covers outer shadows and unsupported table-part backgrounds. | `false`. | | `rasterScale` | Raster pixels per CSS pixel in local regions. | Finite positive number, also bounded by each capture's dimensions and pixel budget. | `2`. | | `verifySource` | Checks that source styles and geometry stay stable. | `'full'` or `'mutations'`; mutations skips CSSOM/computed-style fingerprints and emits `SOURCE_VERIFICATION_REDUCED`. | `'full'`. | | `metadata` | Copies PDF document properties before asynchronous work. | Metadata object below. | Title `'RenderPDF.js'`; other fields omitted. | | `signal` | Cooperative cancellation between export stages. | `AbortSignal`. | Omitted. | | `onWarning` | Observes diagnostic records also retained in the result. | Synchronous `(warning: RenderWarning) => void`. | Omitted; no console logging. | | `onProgress` | Reports stage-local work counts, not elapsed-time percentages. | Synchronous `({ stage, completed, total }) => void`. | Omitted. | `strictCss: false` does not promise support for arbitrary CSS. Supported table borders still render natively. Unsafe layout, missing glyphs and invalid resources still reject. Missing CSS faces reject in `fontMismatch: 'error'` mode; fallback mode reports the substituted face and keeps caller-owned DOM layout. Substituted text inside a raster region rejects with `RASTER_FAILED` for a connected source; use `renderHTML` to relayout a copy before raster capture. Set `strictCss: true` when omitted decoration must fail. Use `fallback` separately to control local raster planning. ### `renderHTML(html, options)` Accepts the `renderPDF` settings above, with these differences and additions. The temporary isolated document and its font faces are released after export. | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `html` | HTML to parse and lay out. Active markup rejects. | Nonempty HTML string; full document in iframe mode, fragment in shadow mode. | Required. | | `fonts` | Programs registered inside the temporary document. | Array of font sources below, without `document`. | Bundled `RenderPDF Base` Noto Sans faces. | | `isolation` | Document parsing or shadow-root fragment; both use a sandboxed iframe. | `'iframe'` or `'shadow'`. | `'iframe'`. | | `sourceWidth` | Browser layout width before PDF fitting. | Finite positive CSS-pixel number, at most `32768`. | Printable width rounded down; `'auto'` orientation uses portrait for initial layout. | | `fontFallback` | Selects a substitute family in fallback mode; copied elements are laid out again and emit `FONT_SUBSTITUTED`. | A family supplied in `fonts`, or bundled `RenderPDF Base`. | Bundled `RenderPDF Base` when fallback is selected. | | `header`, `footer` | Repeated bands in the isolated document. | Text line or slots without a `font` handle, or `{ html, height }`. | Omitted. | ### `registerFont(source)` and font sources | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | | `family` | Explicit CSS family used by the source. | Nonempty supported name; generic families and CSS descriptor injection reject. | Required. | | `data` | Exact licensed font program; input bytes are copied. | `Uint8Array`, `ArrayBuffer`, bare base64 or font data URL containing supported TTF/OTF. | Required. | | `weight` | Declared face weight for font selection. | Integer `1`–`1000`; variable TTF must declare the upright default instance's weight. | `400`. | | `style` | Declared face style. | `'normal'` or `'italic'`; variable TTF supports its upright default instance only. | `'normal'`. | | `document` | Browser document whose `FontFaceSet` owns the registration. Not used by document drawing or accepted by `renderHTML` font sources. | `Document`, usually `element.ownerDocument`. | Current browser document. | System fonts, WOFF/WOFF2, collections and nondefault variable axes are unsupported. Register every used face for exact output. Static weight selection follows CSS nearest-face matching within the registered family; missing glyphs still reject. ### Header and footer fields Each band uses one content form: `text`, `left`/`center`/`right`, `element` for `renderPDF`, or `html` for `renderHTML`. | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | | `height` | Reserved CSS-pixel height in addition to the outer margin. | Finite positive number fitting the band content and leaving positive body space. | Required for a band. | | `text` | One selectable line with page placeholders expanded after pagination. | String; optional `{pageNumber}` and `{pageCount}`. | Required for the single-line form. | | `left`, `center`, `right` | Independent lines at the corresponding horizontal positions. | One or more strings with the same page placeholders; lines must not overlap. | Omitted slots are empty. | | `font` | Exact registered text-band face in `renderPDF`. | A handle included in `fonts`. | First registered face. | | `fontSize` | Text-band character size in CSS pixels. | Finite positive number. | `12`. | | `align` | Alignment of the `text` form. | `'left'`, `'center'` or `'right'`. | `'left'`. | | `element` | Static HTML measured once and repeated as PDF paint. | Connected `HTMLElement` in the source document, outside the source subtree, fitting printable width and band height. | Required for connected HTML. | | `html` | Isolated fragment with its own inline styles; `renderHTML` only. | Nonempty inert HTML; page placeholders are not expanded in HTML. | Required for HTML strings. | ### `imageToPDF(source, options?)` | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | | `source` | Encoded image; main TIFF frames retain file order. | `File`/`Blob`, `ArrayBuffer` or `Uint8Array` containing supported PNG, JPEG or TIFF. | Required. | | `format` | Paper size in CSS pixels. | Same as `renderPDF.format`. | `'A4'`. | | `orientation` | Paper axes. | `'portrait'` or `'landscape'`. | `'portrait'`. | | `margin` | Space around centered, proportionally fitted image content. | Same as `renderPDF.margin`. | `24` on each edge. | | `metadata` | New PDF properties. | Metadata object below. | Title `'RenderPDF.js'`. | | `signal` | Cancels between reading, decoding, embedding and writing. | `AbortSignal`. | Omitted. | | `onProgress` | Stage-local counters; omits HTML `layout`/`pagination`. | Synchronous progress callback. | Omitted. | ### Metadata fields Apply to HTML/image conversion, document creation and PDF composition. | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | ---------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------- | | `title` | Human-readable document title. | Unicode string. | `'RenderPDF.js'`. | | `author` | Author in PDF properties. | Unicode string. | Omitted. | | `subject` | Subject in PDF properties. | Unicode string. | Omitted. | | `keywords` | Search terms copied before export. | Readonly array of strings. | Omitted. | ### `createDocument(options?)` and `createJsPDFAdapter(options?)` | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | `unit` | Coordinate/dimension unit; font sizes remain points. | `'pt'`, `'mm'` or `'px'`. | `'pt'` for documents; `'mm'` for the adapter. | | `format` | Default paper inherited by new pages; custom values use document units. | `'A4'`, `'A3'`, `'Letter'`, or finite positive `{ width, height }`. | `'A4'`. | | `orientation` | Default axes, overridable on each page. | `'portrait'` or `'landscape'`. | `'portrait'`. | | `fonts` | Additional faces prepared before drawing and synchronous measurement. | Font sources with `family`, `data` and optional `weight`/`style`. | Built-in Helvetica, Times and Courier faces. | | `metadata` | New PDF properties. | Metadata object above. | Title `'RenderPDF.js'`. | | `signal` | Cooperative cancellation during preparation and serialization. | `AbortSignal`. | Omitted. | `createDocument` starts without pages; the adapter creates one initial page. `addPage()` and `insertPage()` accept `format` and `orientation` overrides and otherwise inherit document defaults. See the API guide for drawing, fields, graphics state and tested adapter methods. ### `mergePDFs`, `extractPDFPages` and `splitPDF` | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | `sources` / `source` | Existing PDF input; caller fetches URLs. Merge takes an array; extract/split take one input. | `File`/`Blob`, `ArrayBuffer`, `Uint8Array` or result exposing `toUint8Array()`. | Required. | | `pageNumbers` | Extraction order, retaining duplicates. | Nonempty array of valid one-based page numbers. | Required for extraction; merge/split use all pages. | | `flattenForms` | Paints prepared ordinary AcroForm appearances before copying, removing interactivity. | `true` or `false`; signed/XFA forms still reject. | `false`; interactive fields reject. | | `metadata` | New properties; source properties are not merged. | Metadata object above. | Title `'RenderPDF.js'`. | | `signal` | Cancels between loading, copying and saving. | `AbortSignal`. | Omitted. | | `onProgress` | Stage-local preparation/resources/pages/saving/complete counters. | Synchronous progress callback. | Omitted. | See the composition guide for input and structural limits. ### Result output | Name | Info | Allowed settings | Default setting | | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | | `download(filename?)` | Browser download of completed bytes without rerendering. | Nonempty filename without separators or control characters. | `'document.pdf'`. | | `toBlob()` | Returns a Blob from completed bytes. | No parameters. | MIME type `'application/pdf'`. | | `toUint8Array()` | Returns a defensive copy of completed bytes. | No parameters. | New independent array on each call. | `pageCount` and `warnings` are read-only result metadata. Callback exceptions reject the export; cooperative cancellation rejects with `AbortError`. ### Repeated table headers, headers and footers ```ts const pdf = await renderPDF(source, { fonts: [regular], repeatTableHeaders: true, header: { text: 'Account statement', height: 32 }, footer: { height: 28, left: 'Printed by: Example', right: 'Page {pageNumber} of {pageCount}' }, }); await pdf.download('statement.pdf'); ``` Header and footer `height` is required and reserves space **in addition to** the outer margins. Existing `{ text, height, align? }` usage still works. To draw independent selectable text, supply `left`, `center` and/or `right`; each uses the shared `font` (first registered face by default) and `fontSize` (default `12`). `{pageNumber}` and `{pageCount}` expand after pagination. Lines cannot wrap or overlap; a band too small for its content fails explicitly. For custom HTML, connect a separate `HTMLElement` in the source's document and pass `{ element, height }`. It must be outside the main source subtree and fit the printable width and reserved height. The renderer measures this element through the same supported HTML pipeline once, then repeats its PDF text and paint on each page. `renderHTML` also accepts `{ html, height }` strings for bands as shown above. HTML bands are static across pages; use a text slot for page-number placeholders. Custom CSS remains subject to the supported scope. ### Export progress and document properties ```ts const pdf = await renderPDF(source, { fonts: [regular], metadata: { title: 'Account statement', author: 'Example Company' }, onProgress: ({ stage, completed, total }) => { console.log(stage, completed, total); }, }); ``` Counters describe work within the current stage, rather than elapsed-time percentages. HTML stages are `preparing`, `layout`, `pagination`, `resources`, `pages`, `saving` and `complete`. Image conversion omits `layout` and `pagination`. Callbacks are synchronous; a thrown callback error rejects the export. Cancellation is cooperative between stages and rejects with `AbortError`, without a partial PDF. ## Output and errors Both functions return the same result: ```ts await pdf.download('document.pdf'); const blob = await pdf.toBlob(); const bytes = await pdf.toUint8Array(); console.log(pdf.pageCount, pdf.warnings); ``` These output methods reuse the completed PDF. `RenderPDFError`, exported from the package, exposes a `code` and `message` for conversion failures. Warnings are available through `onWarning` for HTML exports and `pdf.warnings`. Unsupported input still fails explicitly when it cannot be represented safely. A missing CSS face throws `MISSING_FONT` in `fontMismatch: 'error'` mode; fallback mode returns `FONT_SUBSTITUTED` through the warning channels and completes if the substitute contains the required glyphs. `MISSING_GLYPH` remains an error in either mode. With the default `strictCss: false`, selected unsupported decoration is omitted as described above. ## Supported scope HTML rendering supports static blocks, inline content, nonoverlapping Flexbox and Grid layouts, horizontal text in the scripts listed below, solid backgrounds, uniform solid borders, simple rounded solid boxes and native tables with `rowspan` and `colspan`. ### Text and languages Horizontal HTML text is verified in Chromium with selectable PDF text for these scripts when the bundled or supplied font covers the characters used: - [x] Latin script, including diacritics - [x] Cyrillic script - [x] Chinese Han text, including line breaks without spaces - [x] Arabic text without vowel marks, including right-to-left and mixed-direction runs Set the source text's `lang` and `dir` where needed, and register suitable font faces for each CSS `font-family`. Other scripts have not been verified. Vertical writing modes are unsupported. HTML export subsets registered TrueType font programs to the glyphs used in the PDF. OpenType/CFF fonts are embedded in full; a large Chinese CFF font can therefore substantially increase PDF size. The programmatic document API requests subsetting for embedded fonts. Arabic vowel marks render, but PDF text extraction can move a mark around a ligature; vocalized Arabic is not yet covered by the selectable-text guarantee. PNG/JPEG resources can use data, blob, same-origin or CORS-readable URLs. External images may be fetched by the browser; documents are never sent to a conversion service. Freshly fetched image bytes receive the same structural, dimension and PNG decompression checks as standalone image input. PNG/JPEG orientation in HTML must be absent or `1`; normalize rotated pixels before using an ` ` element. Simple rounded boxes with a solid background and uniform solid border are drawn as PDF paths, keeping descendant text selectable. Rounded boxes with other effects, gradients, inline bitmap backgrounds, inset shadows and opacity can use local raster fallback on supported rectangular blocks. `data-raster` selects a region explicitly. Regions are captured once in paint order; descendant text gets an extraction layer where safe. Raster resources must be inline bitmaps; responsive images (` `, ` ` and `img[srcset]`), external resources, transforms and backdrop effects are unsupported. Outer shadows on native elements and selected raster roots are omitted by default; `strictCss: true` rejects them. Outer shadows on descendants inside an existing raster region still reject. WebKit's SVG image painter drops inset box shadows. The raster fallback preserves a single sharp, rectangular inset stroke without an existing border by painting an equivalent inner outline in its temporary clone. Other inset shadows in WebKit, including blurred, layered or descendant inset shadows, fail with `RASTER_FAILED` rather than silently producing incomplete pixels. Inline event handlers and custom elements, including customized built-ins, are rejected before capture so cloning cannot repeat their application callbacks. Wrapped inline backgrounds or borders require a containing raster region; inline and table-internal raster boundaries are unsupported. ### Pagination and tables The default `pageBreak: 'css'` respects block/table-row `break-before: page`, `break-after: page`, their legacy `page-break-*: always` aliases and `break-inside: avoid/avoid-page`. Before/after avoidance keeps adjacent complete block siblings together when they fit. Text lines, images, raster regions, table rows and spanning cells stay whole. Content taller than a page, or a forced break through an indivisible item, fails with `PAGINATION_FAILED`. An avoid preference that cannot be honored can be relaxed with a `BREAK_AVOID_RELAXED` warning. Parity/column breaks, inline/cell break rules, widow/orphan policies and cloned page decorations are unsupported. Table restrictions Collapsed tables support solid, none and hidden borders on cells and the outer table, including different widths, colors and transparency. Shared borders are painted once. Row, row-group, column and column-group border contributions, other border styles, captions, nested collapsed tables and altered table-part display modes are unsupported. Repeated headers require a visible native `thead` followed by body rows. The header reserves space on continuation pages and stays with the first body row. Headers and rows must fit on a page. Nested tables, raster headers, overlapping table ranges, header rowspans and cells spanning the header/body boundary are unsupported. Header paint must fit its measured box. Table footers are not repeated. Collapsed tables also require matching resolved horizontal borders at every possible header/body continuation boundary. ### Text and layout limits Default kerning, ligatures and combining marks are supported. Keep shaped text runs in one text node; cross-inline ligatures and zero-width fragments are unsupported. Custom font features/variants, stretched faces, font-size adjustment, automatic hyphenation and soft hyphens are unsupported. Exact text appearance can vary between shaping engines. Arbitrary CSS stacking and overlapping paint are unsupported. Pause animations and keep source styles, geometry and registered fonts stable during export. Changes to the source fail with `SOURCE_CHANGED`. `verifySource: 'mutations'` is an explicit faster mode that checks observed DOM/stylesheet mutations but can miss CSSOM edits and computed-style-only changes; it emits `SOURCE_VERIFICATION_REDUCED`. ### Image format limits - **PNG:** static images only; APNG is rejected. - **JPEG:** 8-bit baseline, extended and progressive grayscale, RGB or CMYK. - **TIFF:** classic stripped TIFF in either byte order; common bilevel/grayscale, palette and 8-bit RGB/RGBA profiles. Compression: uncompressed, CCITT RLE/Group 3/Group 4, LZW, PackBits and Deflate. Limited to **40 million pixels per frame** and **1,000 main frames**. BigTIFF, tiled TIFF, SubIFDs/RAW layouts, planar-separated samples, 16-bit/float samples and JPEG-compressed TIFF fail with `UNSUPPORTED_IMAGE`. The TIFF decoder uses a bounded packed-raster implementation for CCITT runs; the remaining TIFF codec/color-conversion dependency loads only when needed. Structural checks reject malformed input, but cannot identify every damaged JPEG scan or all possible unsupported image features. ### Existing PDF input limits Composition checks the input container before the PDF backend loads it. Each object/xref stream may expand to at most **2 MiB**, with **16 MiB** total decoded structural streams, **100,000 structural entries**, **2 million container tokens** and **64 levels of container nesting** per composition. Page and form ownership trees must be acyclic, consistent and at most 64 levels deep. The existing 1,000-page and encoded-input limits also apply. The supported profile requires a standalone PDF header line at byte zero, unsigned decimal structural indexes, uppercase hexadecimal name escapes, direct stream lengths and direct stream types when present. Object/xref streams support no filter or one direct `FlateDecode` filter without decoding parameters. Indirect control values, duplicate dictionary keys and unsupported structural filters fail with `INVALID_SOURCE`. Some otherwise valid PDFs therefore need normalization by their owner before composition. Additional/chained page, annotation and form actions are rejected; copied URI links support HTTP, HTTPS, mailto and tel only. Composition preserves PDF paint and resources and is not a general sanitizer for every PDF viewer feature. ## Development Use Node.js 22.18+ (22.x), 24.11+ (24.x) or 26+. `.node-version` records the verified runtime. ```sh npm ci npm run build npm run check ``` `npm run check` runs formatting, lint, types, unit tests, browser tests, build and package checks. Google Chrome must be available for browser tests, either as an installed app or through `RENDERPDF_CHROME_EXECUTABLE`. Vite+ provides the development toolchain; Playwright and PDF.js are used for testing. `npm run test:cross-browser` runs the focused Edge, Firefox and WebKit matrix; its browser prerequisites and limits are in tests/README.md. Run `npm run dev` to serve synthetic test fixtures. The independent playground tests the packaged library. See the benchmark guide for `npm run benchmark` and timing reports. To create a local package, create `artifacts/` if needed, then run `npm pack --pack-destination artifacts`. Only the library build, declarations, package metadata, README, API guide, changelog, license and logo are packaged. Keep private documents and generated files out of Git. ## License MIT. Third-party dependencies retain their own licenses: `utif2` uses MIT and `pako` retains MIT/Zlib notices. Noto Sans, Noto Serif, Arabic and CJK test fonts retain the SIL Open Font License and are not included in the npm package. See tests/README.md for commands, coverage by file, verification methods and remaining coverage limits. # MantissaLabs/mantissa

title: Show HN: Gradual Daylight Saving – Spread the 1-hour shifts over the whole year
author: johndimm
body: Instead of jumping an hour twice a year, shift a little bit each day. The offset rises smoothly from 0 at winter solstice to +60 minutes at summer solstice and back. Max daily change is ~32 seconds.William Willett's original 1907 proposal was actually 8 shifts of 20 minutes —- four forward in spring, four back in autumn. Gentler on humans than what we ended up with. Now that most clocks are networked, there's no reason to stop at 8.The site has an interactive demo with two clocks (official vs. smooth), a year-long offset chart, and a working Smooth Time clock you can use as an alarm. Built with Next.js.

title: Show HN: PewPewPew – Multiplayer Asteroids with deterministic rollback at 60hz
author: Benjaminsen
body: I have been building realtime multiplayer games that run in a browser since 1999 and my latest is pewpewpew.io which combines everything I know about doing this well.The game uses a fully client and server synchronized state machine running at 60hz with rollback / rollforward on both client and server.During normal play only user input is transmitted using a compressed message format, where input is 7 fields in 2 bytes, with a total of about 26KB/s used for a room with 32 active players.Users are automatically distributed into a room on a server with the lowest measured ping where there are other players playing.Currently running using cloudflare Durable Objects, but I expect to offload it to dedicated metal should the cost go above $500 / month. Current monthly cost sits at about $300 per 1K average CCU.Works on mobile, free to play, no ads, no signup.

title: Show HN: HackerBooks – HackerTube, but for books mentioned on HN
author: roansh
body: Saw Karpathy's HackerTube and wanted the same thing for books. So I had Claude build one (Opus 5.5).It's ~16.5k books that at least two different HN commenters brought up, from 2007 till now. Each book links back to the comments that mentioned it. Data is downloadable from the about page.To be clear: Claude wrote almost all of it, including the data pipeline and the site. I mostly steered and made calls, bought the domain name, etc.It counts mentions, so it's not perfect (praising a book and trashing it both count). If your favourite book is missing or matched to the wrong thing, tell me.

title: Show HN: Sweet-search – local code search for agents (5–33% cheaper runs)
author: mrsladoje
body:
Hi everyone :)After almost a year of fighting windmills, I am proud to say I built sweet-search, a local code search tool for Claude Code, Codex and Opencode.It delivers 5-33% cheaper agentic runs with Sol 6.1 and Opus 5.5 with Claude Code, Codex and Opencode, with pooled solved tasks equal vs native (both 481 of 1,000 tasks pooled on 5 model*harness combos). 
Measured on 200 held-out SWE-rebench tasks. 
Detailed bench results are in the README.It consists of 6 tools: hybrid search with late interaction reranking, my version of grep, and others.
It also has GPU accelerated indexing (for embedding and late interaction models) and low footprint incremental indexing.Some highlights:
1. The ANN kernel is custom and very competitive with FAISS and USearch.
2. The custom MaxSim kernel is 1.4–7.3× faster than NumPy and PyTorch (reranking on CPU).
3. My hybrid-search tool is SOTA on M2CRB and zero-shot SOTA on CoSQA.
4. My custom grep tool is 2.46x faster e2e than ripgrep and ranks hits in a specific way (inspired by Sainte-Laguë).Here is the promo video I built with fframes and Opus 5.5: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lJzgXRQprs4Would love to hear your opinions,
Marko :)

## Top Contributors

- abronan (1203 contributions)

---

## README

 
 
 

---

Mantissa is a distributed orchestration system that grows with you and your workloads.
Every node participates equally in scheduling, state replication, and cluster membership.
No control-plane masters, and no federation layer required at scale. The focus of Mantissa
is convergence and auto-stabilization.

Built in Rust with Cap'n Proto RPC, CRDT replication, Merkle Search Trees over Redb, and
an eBPF driven data path, Mantissa targets low-latency scheduling and fault-tolerant
operation across small and large fleets of nodes alike.

## Why Mantissa?

Traditional workload orchestration systems often rely on a centralized control plane, which
could become a bottleneck and hard to maintain as the cluster grows. Mantissa explores an alternative
approach that leverages distributed scheduling with optimistic concurrency. It is similar to the
Omega scheduler in the
approach, but with the shared state being replicated via CRDTs.

The goal is to reduce the operational overhead and complexity, simplifying upgrades and maintenance
as well as aiming for a highly available and fault-tolerant system. This could be useful to scale
infrastructures and deploy a large number of AI agents for example.

## Status

**Experimental**. Do not use in production (_yet_).

Take this as a research-focused system, pushing the scalability limits of a completely distributed
control plane.

See the docs/limits.md for more details on the ongoing challenges and limitations.

## Highlights

- Fully distributed scheduling with resource reservation (no primary scheduler).
- Designed to scale to large fleets of nodes without a federation layer.
- Various workload types with their own lifecycles: _services_ (tasks), _jobs_ and _agents_.
- Batch placement, opt-in gang admission, and dependency-aware rollout for multi-task services.
- GPU-aware scheduling with device-level reservations (NVIDIA).
- eBPF-accelerated overlay networking for low-latency service discovery and routing.
- Durable state via CRDT + Merkle Search Tree (backed by Redb) for fault tolerance and convergence.
- Support for cluster split/merge operations (creating cluster views).
- Cluster dataplane encryption using Noise, vxlan traffic encrypted via wireguard.

## Local cluster experimentation (Dev Cluster)

1. Provision a local multi-VM cluster with Lima:

Install lima, clone the mantissa repository and navigate to the project directory, then:

```bash
./setup-dev-cluster.sh -n 3 -r $(pwd)
```

2. Open a shell into each VM with the repo as the working directory:

```bash
limactl shell --workdir /mantissa mantissa-1
```

Then build once on one of the VMs:

```bash
cargo build
```

3. Start the first node and grab its join token:

```bash
sudo mantissa init
mantissa token show
```

`mantissa init` prompts for the local master-key envelope passphrase when run
interactively. Non-interactive deployments should provide it through
`--master-key-passphrase-file` or `--master-key-passphrase-fd`.
Use `mantissa init --detach` to run the local daemon in the background; it
still prompts when attached to a terminal. Inspect it with `mantissa status`,
stream daemon logs with `mantissa logs -f`, and stop it with
`mantissa shutdown`.

4. Join a second node (replace ` ` and ` `):

```bash
sudo mantissa init
mantissa join --anchor <vm1-ip>:6578 --join-token <TOKEN>
```

5. Submit commands on the cluster (_from any node_) and try out the examples:

```bash
mantissa nodes list
mantissa services run examples/service_discovery_demo.ron
mantissa networks list
mantissa services list
mantissa tasks list
mantissa tasks logs <id-task>
```

6. Play around and bring nodes up/down (_see the rebalanced tasks, and the network/attachments healing_)

---

- See docs/quickstart.md for the full local and multi-VM workflow.

## Contributing

See CONTRIBUTING.md.

comments.text:
Hello HN,I’m Alexandre, I have worked on Docker Swarm and the integration with distributed key value stores (etcd/consul/zookeeper), but also on Docker Swarmkit and the Raft distributed datastore, with the integration of etcd's Raft library.Last July, I open sourced Mantissa (https://mantissa.io): a fully distributed scheduler and container orchestrator. I did this quietly to keep working on patches and stability. It is still at an experimental stage and will probably stay that way for a while, but could be tested to get a "look and feel" of the project.Mantissa is using CRDTs[1] and Merkle Search Trees[2] for its data replication strategy (via anti-entropy/gossip). It is a bit of a departure from existing systems that are relying on strong consistency/linearizability (like Kubernetes, Swarm and Nomad): Mantissa focuses on fast convergence and self-stabilization instead. This comes with plenty of benefits (no quorum and Primary/Follower setup, simplified deployment and upgrades, etc.) but also trade-offs (increased storage size, no resource overcommit, temporary divergences in or outside of partition events, etc.) that would be too long to list and detail here.Mantissa is a particular fit for small clusters, home labs, agent orchestration but could also be used in larger settings (I’d be comfortable to say up to a hundred nodes per cluster view/shard, but I’m making no claims for higher than this, since I don’t yet have access to hardware that would allow me to test and make such a claim). At the core was the idea that it should be trivial to interconnect machines together and create a transparent overlay on top of the operating system, regardless of the scale.It is sort of a spiritual successor to Docker Swarmkit: going even further with simplification and reducing the deployment and maintenance burden. You'll see that it retains some of its design elements (with the node join flow) while taking inspiration from other systems like Google Omega[3].Why building Mantissa while Kubernetes and other systems exist? I think it is worthwhile to experiment with new approaches and see how it may impact existing systems. Improving on the UX/DX of schedulers and orchestrators has been a long obsession of mine and Mantissa is a long story, with its initial codebase and architecture being 10 years old. The scope is incredibly large however and working on this alone is quite difficult even with the help of LLMs. AI is a double-edged sword, and I could write a full article around my frustrations with building complex distributed systems with LLMs (they have a hard time “reasoning” correctly about systems relying on convergence for example).I’m having a lot of fun building this however and I hope this could be useful to some of you, despite its current limitations and experimental status. Feedback is also welcome to help steer the project in a direction where it could be the most useful/impactful to you.Cheers.Github: https://github.com/MantissaLabs/mantissa[1] https://www.lip6.fr/Marc.Shapiro/papers/RR-7687.pdf
[2] https://inria.hal.science/hal-02303490/file/paper%20%281%29....
[3] https://research.google/pubs/omega-flexible-scalable-schedul...

comments.author: abronan
comments.text: It’s a fair concern, and Mantissa is really just moving the complexity around.One detail is that it relies on Strong Eventual Consistency, which is a slightly stronger model than Eventual Consistency. Replicas that have observed the same updates are guaranteed to converge to the same end state, regardless of the order in which those updates have been received.That said, convergence alone doesn’t guarantee scheduling correctness. This is why it separates convergence from scheduling coordination. The CRDTs and MSTs provide the replicated state, and the scheduling protocol handles placement decisions and conflicting operations (with atomic slot reservation that is node local). There is a reconciliation loop (owned by a single node that is picked for the service/workload to deploy) that is then responsible for bringing the cluster back to its desired state if it potentially made a wrong call.And it comes with trade-offs as mentioned in my post. You accept temporary divergences rather than requiring global agreement before every operation. This may or may not be acceptable for certain workloads. This removes the need for a quorum-based and centralized control plane, but it also means that certain invariants and guarantees have to be enforced at the scheduling and workload layer rather than by the datastore itself.Strong consistency is also not a silver bullet to handle distributed systems. It is relatively hard to get it right and not serve stale values because of the presence of bugs in the protocol or state corruption. It could also bring the availability down and prevent from scheduling any more tasks due to a loss of quorum (which is by design and acceptable in most cases).Mantissa is just making a different trade-off and accepting a different set of problems to solve: favoring availability and accepting that the desired state could shift temporarily on partition and network blips. If your cluster has good connectivity, then it should be a rare event, for which you should have prepared with some replicas that could handle being moved around. Again, it is not for everybody, and will probably remain a niche tool for users who want a simplified cluster deployment/updates to schedule mostly stateless tasks (even though stateful tasks are supported).One remaining comment: replicated volumes do use a Raft quorum per volume. There are things that couldn't accept anything weaker than strong consistency, and volumes are one of them. So we are using strong eventual consistency for most of the state replication, but fallback to Raft for things that truly require strong consistency.

# Bowerbird

An open-source NotebookLM alternative where your files stay yours and every quote is checked.

Add PDFs, books, web pages, YouTube videos and recordings, then ask questions. Answers cite the passages they draw on, and each quoted phrase is looked up in the source it cites. Notebooks are plain folders on your disk, search, OCR and speech run on your machine, and answers come from any model you choose.

## Every quote is checked

Each citation in an answer carries the words it quotes. Bowerbird looks those words up in the source the citation names: in the cited passage, or in another passage of the same source, since a quote can run across a passage boundary. A quote that isn't there, or that the answer attributes to the wrong source, is marked unverified, and the footer counts how many were found. A quote shortened with an ellipsis counts only when each of its pieces is long enough to stand on its own and the pieces sit close together.

The check shows that the quoted words are in the source, not that the answer reads them correctly. Click a citation to open the passage with the quoted words highlighted, or, for a PDF, the printed page, and judge for yourself.

## What leaves your machine

Notebooks, the search index, OCR, transcription and the voices of audio overviews stay on your machine. Bowerbird sends no analytics and doesn't check for updates. This is everything that goes out:

| What | Where it goes | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your question, the earlier turns of that conversation, and the parts of your sources found for it | The model provider you choose, DeepSeek by default | Each question |
| The parts of your sources behind the notebook's overview | The same model provider | When you open a notebook whose sources changed |
| The parts of your sources a report or study material draws on | The same model provider | Each time you make one |
| A link you add | That website, and the sites its pictures are on | When you add it |
| A YouTube video you add | YouTube, for the video's captions | When you add it |
| A web search for sources | The search service set in Settings: your own SearXNG, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Tavily or Exa | Each search |
| Requests for the local models | Hugging Face and GitHub; each file is checked against its recorded SHA-256 | Each model's first use |

API keys go only to their own provider. Choose an Ollama model running on your machine, and questions and passages stay there too.

## What it does

- Sources: PDF, Word (.docx), EPUB, Markdown, plain text, web pages, YouTube captions, and audio recordings, which are transcribed on your machine with Whisper. Scanned PDFs are read with OCR on your machine (PP-OCRv5, Latin script including accented letters; Cyrillic and other scripts aren't read yet). Pictures in web pages, Word documents and EPUBs are kept beside their captions.
- Search by keyword and by meaning: passages are found with SQLite FTS5 (BM25) and with EmbeddingGemma vectors, fused by weighted reciprocal rank, so a question worded differently from the source still finds it. Questions can be asked in a different language from the sources.
- Notes: save answers to notes, edit them, and add a note back as a source.
- Reports: a study guide, briefing, timeline, FAQ, or a report you describe, written into a note with citations.
- Study material: flashcards (with Anki export), quizzes, mind maps (SVG), data tables (CSV), slide decks (PPTX), infographics (SVG, PNG), and audio overviews in four formats, voiced on your machine with Kokoro.
- Finding sources: search the web through DuckDuckGo, SearXNG, Brave, Tavily or Exa, and add what you pick.
- Runs where you work: a web app served from your machine, a desktop app for Linux, macOS and Windows, and an Android app. Light and dark themes.

 

## Download

Builds for Linux (`.deb`, AppImage), macOS 13.4 or later (Apple Silicon `.dmg`), Windows (portable `.zip`) and Android (64-bit ARM `.apk`) are attached to each release. The macOS app is signed ad hoc, not notarized, so macOS blocks its first launch: allow it under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Open Anyway. To build from source, see Build and run.

## How it works

1. A source is extracted to text with its heading tree: PDF bookmarks or font sizes, HTML and Markdown headings, EPUB and Word structure. Scanned PDFs and recordings are first read by OCR or Whisper in the background.
2. The text is split into passages and indexed in SQLite with FTS5. The source is searchable as soon as that finishes.
3. In the background, each passage gets an EmbeddingGemma vector. Until a passage has one, keyword search answers alone.
4. A question's keyword hits and nearest passages by meaning are fused, each hit brings its neighbors in the same section, and a source that ranks among the candidates gets its best passage even if it misses the top 8. Deep search also lets the model pick whole sections from the outline.
5. The model answers with citations to passage labels such as `B12`, and each quoted span is matched against that passage's text.

## Models

The default model is `deepseek-flash`. Any provider that genai supports works, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter and Ollama. In Settings, enter the model name (prefix it with the provider, as in `groq::model-name`, to choose the provider yourself) and paste the provider's API key.

Keys are saved in `settings.toml`, readable only by your user account: `~/.config/bowerbird/` on Linux and macOS, `%APPDATA%\bowerbird\` on Windows, or the path in `$BOWERBIRD_CONFIG`. A key set as an environment variable, such as `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, works too.

The local models download on first use into `~/.local/share/bowerbird/models` (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\bowerbird\models` on Windows): EmbeddingGemma 4-bit for search (200 MB) when the first source is added, the OCR models (12 MB) for the first scanned PDF, and the speech models when they are first used. Their licenses, including the Gemma Terms of Use that cover EmbeddingGemma, are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

## Your data

Each notebook is a folder in `~/Bowerbird`, or in `$BOWERBIRD_HOME`:

```
<notebook>/
  notebook.toml            title, answer style, sources (order, letters)
  sources/                 originals as added, plus OCR text and transcripts
  notes/<id>.md            Markdown notes
  chats/<id>.jsonl         one conversation: questions, answers, citations
  studio/<id>.json         flashcards, quizzes and other study material
  guide.json               overview and suggested questions
  .bowerbird/index.sqlite  search index and vectors, rebuilt when missing

```

Copying the folder backs up or moves the notebook.

## Build and run

Needs Rust 1.95 or newer and Node.js 22.17 or newer. On Debian or Ubuntu, install the build tools and the desktop app's libraries first:

```
sudo apt-get install cmake clang libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev
```

```
scripts/fetch-pdfium.sh                  # PDFium, which reads PDFs, into vendor/pdfium
export BOWERBIRD_PDFIUM_DIR="$PWD/vendor/pdfium/lib"
npm --prefix ui ci
npm --prefix ui run build
cargo run --release -p bowerbird-server
```

The server prints a link with an access token. Open it in a browser. It listens on `127.0.0.1:7477`; `--addr` changes that, and anything other than a loopback address exposes your notebooks to the network, protected only by the token. Links added through the server may only point at the public internet, not at the server's own machine or its local network, unless it runs with `--allow-private-links`. Leave that off when anyone else can reach the server, directly or through a reverse proxy. The desktop app allows such links.

### Command line

The `bowerbird` command works on the same library:

```
cargo run --release -p bowerbird -- add history treaty.pdf https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peace_of_Westphalia
cargo run --release -p bowerbird -- ask history "Who signed the treaty at Osnabrück?"
```

### Desktop app

On Linux, install Tauri's prerequisites, then:

```
ui/node_modules/.bin/tauri build --config crates/desktop/tauri.conf.json
```

The `.deb` and AppImage land in `target/release/bundle/`. On a Mac with Apple Silicon, run `scripts/fetch-pdfium.sh` first and add `--bundles app,dmg`; the `.dmg` lands in `target/release/bundle/dmg/`.

The Windows app cross-compiles from Linux with cargo-xwin (needs clang 19 or newer, lld and llvm):

```
scripts/windows.sh
```

The portable folder lands in `dist/bowerbird-windows`: `Bowerbird.exe` with `DirectML.dll`, `pdfium\pdfium.dll` and the licenses beside it.

### Android

```
scripts/android.sh
```

Builds a 64-bit ARM APK. Needs the Android SDK and NDK, found through `ANDROID_HOME` and `NDK_HOME`. The APK is signed with the release key that `crates/desktop/gen/android/keystore.properties` names (`storeFile`, relative to that folder, `keyAlias` and `password`; kept out of git), or with the debug key when that file is missing.

## Tests

```
cargo test --workspace
npm --prefix ui run check
ui/node_modules/.bin/playwright install chromium     # once
cargo build -p bowerbird-server && npm --prefix ui run test:e2e
BOWERBIRD_LIVE=1 cargo test -p bowerbird-core --test live
BOWERBIRD_LIVE=1 cargo test -p bowerbird-core --lib -- "ocr::" "embed::" "retrieve::"
```

The end-to-end tests and the live test ask the default model real questions, so they need `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. The end-to-end tests serve the UI from `ui/build`, so build it first. The live test also checks YouTube captions, web page extraction and DuckDuckGo; the last line downloads the OCR and search models and reads a scanned page.

`node ui/scripts/readme-screenshots.mjs docs/screenshots` rebuilds the demo notebook and the screenshots above. Run it against a server whose `--library` is an empty folder; it asks the configured model real questions.

### Continuous integration

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, on every push and pull request: formatting, clippy with warnings as errors, the workspace tests, the UI type check, and `cargo deny` for licenses (`deny.toml`) and advisories.
- `.github/workflows/live.yml`, daily: the live tests and the end-to-end tests. Needs the `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` repository secret.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`, on `v*` tags and manual runs: the Linux, macOS, Windows and Android builds; a tag publishes them as a GitHub release. It also runs weekly without macOS, whose runner minutes cost ten times as much. The APK gets the release key from the `ANDROID_KEYSTORE` (base64 of the keystore) and `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` repository secrets.

## License

MIT. The software by others in the releases, and the models the app downloads, are listed with their licenses in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. ARCHITECTURE.md describes how the code fits together, CONTRIBUTING.md how to send a change, and SECURITY.md how to report a vulnerability.

# Don't just see the trade. Investigate the story.

Press ✦ Spy on any insider trade on InsiderPrint. Seven checks run on public SEC filings and our measured history, and you get the evidence for it, the evidence against it, and a plain list of what we couldn't check.

## This week's insider buys: pick one to investigate

Open-market purchases filed in the last 7 days, largest first.

| Stock | Insider | Filed | Bought | Investigate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CRBG Corebridge Financial, Inc. | Nippon Life Insurance Co 10% Owner | Oct 27, 2026 | $13.9M | ✦ Spy on this trade |
| DOLE Dole plc | Pale Fire Capital Se 10% Owner | Oct 22, 2026 | $5.8M | ✦ Spy on this trade |

## The seven checks

Each one lights up only after it has actually run.

1 · Finding the SEC filing The Form 4 behind the trade: who, role, trade date, filing date, shares, price, and the link to the original.

2 · Reading the filing's qualifiers Pre-planned 10b5-1 sales, shares held through a trust or fund, late filings, amendments, prices that looked like typos.

3 · This insider's own history Their earlier buys and sales here: is this their first purchase, or several times their usual size?

4 · What other insiders did Everyone else buying or selling the same stock in the last 90 days, and how much of the selling was pre-planned.

5 · Similar past buys Buys since 2020 with the same traits, how often they beat the S&P 500, and real best and worst examples.

6 · What happened after The stock 7, 30 and 90 days after this filing, against the S&P 500. "Pending" until the days pass.

Most insider-trading sites give you a headline like “a director bought $2M in shares.” We never get more or better context, like :Is this normal for this person?Were other insiders selling?Was the trade pre-planned?How did similar buys actually turn out?For example: when a CEO buys their own stock, did buys like that beat the S&P 500 afterwards?So I built https://www.insiderprint.com/spy-mode. Press it on any insider trade and it checks:The SEC filing itselfThe filing’s fine print: pre-planned 10b5-1 trades, shares held indirectly, late filingsThe insider’s own trading historyWhat other insiders did in the last 90 daysSimilar past buys since 2020How the stock did afterwards against the S&P 500The evidence for and againstIn my data, only about 46%” (add “over the next 90 days” at the end)Again the idea is to give more context on each trade based on the history and patterns and how it impacted everytime on the stock value. 
This is not a financial advice tool :) and it is free :)There are many interesting tools like Time Machine or same board members have made similar trades at other companies whose boards they sit on.I’d love to hear what other checks you’d want it to run

title: Show HN: Shroom – screen recording and sharing, your own Cloudflare, 10M setup
author: _bagrat
body: Some months I needed to record and share a single 30-minute demo, but in other months I only needed a few 2-minute quick videos. Paying $18/month didn't justify. So I had to build it myself.Shroom is a free, open source (MIT) screen recording and sharing app for Mac, hosted in your own Cloudflare account. Install with one line (or with your AI agent) and follow a guided setup for about 10 minutes, a few clicks (create a token, add a card to enable storage on Cloudflare).With Cloudflare's free tier, up to about 3 hours of recorded videos cost you nothing. After that, it is still cheap - use the slider at https://shroom.am to see the approximate storage costs.Shroom auto-deletes stale videos (old, unwatched) to keep your storage consumption low. Pin important videos to keep them from being deleted.Invite your teammates with a single link, they don't need a Cloudflare account. Their videos go into your storage. You only pay for storage, no matter how many people you invite.It comes with an editor, but you can also cut as you record. If you make a mistake, just say "shroom cut" while recording and continue. After you stop the slipped sentence will be cut for you. It will also add chapters and captions to your video using AI, again, all running in your Cloudflare.Github: https://github.com/bagrat/shroom

title: Show HN: Breath of the Wild's Hyrule digital diorama
author: jsomau
body: Two weeks ago I posted a Zelda timeline here ahead of the Ocarina of Time remake. Here's what I've been working on: Breath of the Wild's Hyrule as a small 3D diorama you can explore. It has the main landmarks and a few easter eggs. It was the last Zelda game I played, early in the pandemic on a Wii U. It's been a fun little hit of nostalgia revisiting those places.The terrain information comes from data the Zelda modding community which was then smoothed and scaled down. It's Three.js with the lighting and shadows baked when the page loads.I built it with Claude, as I did the timeline. Without it, I'd never have had the time for a project this whimsical, so it wouldn't have seen the light of day. I didn't write any of the code. For me it felt a lot like part of being a tech lead: shaping the ideas and the output.
